notes: Only one tool is advertised (`fetch`, server.py:200-206); a `fetch` prompt also exists (server.py:257-284) but prompts are not tools.

httpx's default transport supports http/https only, so `file://` URLs are unlikely to be readable despite `AnyUrl` accepting them; SECRET rests on loopback/intranet HTTP reachability, which is unrestricted.

fetch.rationale: `call_tool` passes the agent-supplied `url` straight to `fetch_url`, which issues `client.get(url, follow_redirects=True)` with no host/scheme allow-list, no private-IP or loopback filtering (server.py:119-126). The response body is returned into the agent context (server.py:255), so arbitrary attacker-controlled web pages become agent input (UNTRUSTED), and any reachable `localhost`/intranet HTTP endpoint the host can talk to is read back to the agent (SECRET). Because the full URL, including query string and path, is agent-chosen, the tool is also an exfiltration channel to an attacker-controlled host (SINK). The only gate is the robots.txt check in `check_may_autonomously_fetch_url`, which an attacker controls on their own host and which does not protect internal endpoints (a 4xx robots.txt simply returns, server.py:92-93). No code execution on the host.

value_conditions.effect: Skips the robots.txt permission check entirely; with the flag off (default) the check still runs but is attacker-controlled for attacker-owned hosts and returns early on 4xx robots.txt, so it removes no label.
Routes all fetches through the given proxy; does not restrict reachable destinations so labels are unchanged.
Overrides the User-Agent header sent with requests; no effect on reach or labels.
